value.rationale: The two-coordinate half-quasinorm ball is the simplest nonconvex sparsity constraint allowing a nontrivial projection fiber. A complete exact phase portrait yields two structural thresholds, a sharp square-root sensitivity law, support collapse, and impossibility of continuous local selections at all post-threshold diagonal targets. These facts inform the robustness of projected sparse algorithms.
